predictions: The variant will not produce a reproducible TF-dependent change in TERT expression; any association may reflect another cause or a linked alteration.

chains.title: Candidate GABPA-mediated increase in TERT promoter activity

links.claim: Hypothesis: the alt allele binds GABPA more strongly. GABPA is the leading candidate because the literature mentions GABPA-augmented identification of a TERT promoter mutation and ETS motif gains, and GABPA peaks overlap this site in other biosamples. This does not establish the allele direction or occupancy in glioblastoma: no allele-specific binding result or QBiC-SELEX result/model is supplied, and no matching U-87 MG peak is reported.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE, but its reported chromatin signals are maxima across biosamples rather than glioblastoma-specific measurements.
TERT is the nearest annotated gene and the variant is upstream of its transcript; this makes TERT a candidate target but does not show regulation by this variant.
Glioblastoma is a proposed context based on the supplied expression context, but matching GABPA occupancy and cCRE activity are not established.

If this mechanism increases TERT activity, it could be relevant to tumor biology. The cited literature supports broader relevance of TERT promoter mutations in glioblastoma and melanoma, not this GABPA mechanism or a mechanism in bladder disease.

predictions: In an appropriate glioblastoma context, the alt allele will show greater GABPA binding and higher TERT promoter activity than ref; reducing GABPA will diminish the allele-dependent activity difference.
The predicted effect will depend on GABPA rather than MAX or JUN.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays show no greater GABPA binding to alt, or the allele-dependent TERT expression effect persists when GABPA is reduced.

checks.why: Variant-specific quoted evidence for allele-dependent binding or reporter effects could materially strengthen or redirect the binding and downstream mechanism ranking.
Checks whether the reported GABPA occupancy extends to a glioblastoma cell line at the variant site; occupancy alone would not establish the alt-versus-ref direction.

args.query: TERT C250T allele-specific TF binding reporter assay GABPA MAX JUN glioblastoma

matrix.test: Compare ref and alt TERT-promoter reporters in a glioblastoma cell line with control versus GABPA depletion; measure reporter activity.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent activity difference, or any difference is not specifically reduced by GABPA depletion.
Alt reporter activity exceeds ref with control treatment, and the difference is reduced by GABPA depletion.
No specific GABPA-dependent difference; a reporter effect, if present, should instead depend on MAX.
No specific GABPA-dependent difference; a reporter effect, if present, should instead depend on JUN.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific GABPA occupancy at the variant in a suitable heterozygous glioblastoma model, with allele-aware CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq.

outcomes.outcome: Greater GABPA occupancy on alt than ref.
No specific prediction of alt-enriched GABPA occupancy.
No specific prediction of alt-enriched GABPA occupancy.

matrix.test: Use isogenic base editing to exchange ref and alt in glioblastoma cells; measure TERT expression with and without the predicted TF perturbation.

outcomes.outcome: Editing produces no reproducible TF-dependent TERT expression change.
Alt increases TERT expression relative to ref, and the increase is reduced by GABPA perturbation.
Any editing-associated TERT change is reduced by MAX perturbation rather than GABPA perturbation.
Any editing-associated TERT change is reduced by JUN perturbation rather than GABPA perturbation.

next_experiment: Compare ref and alt TERT-promoter reporters in a glioblastoma cell line with and without GABPA depletion. This is the cheapest proposed test that directly distinguishes the leading GABPA-mediated chain from the null by asking whether an alt-associated activity increase depends on GABPA.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.

Conclusions: Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
The genetic landscape of familial melanoma is heterogeneous.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
BackgroundMutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

ConclusionThe rs2853669 C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
The prognostic relevance of CDKN2A deletion may vary according to TERTp status, particularly for OS.
